rows.global_ob_bundling: Centene bundles routine OB care; separate pregnancy E/M excluded, second twin billable with modifier 51.
Global OB bundle CPTs are not recognized after 1/1/2027; same-day postpartum is bundled to delivery.
01967 primary; 01968/01969 reimbursed separately as add-ons with separate time, not combined.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Routine global obstetric care is bundled when the same physician or group provides antepartum, delivery, and postpartum services. For vaginal twin delivery, the policy allows a higher-complexity global maternity claim with modifier 22.

pairing_conditions: same physician or group provides global care
third- or fourth-degree laceration at delivery
exemptions: state, contractual, or health plan policy exception
modifier 22 may be warranted if documented

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Healthfirst's obstetric billing policy is on-topic for delivery episodes but does not adjudicate this DRG label directly. It requires delivery modifiers U7/U8/U9, treats same-day postpartum care as part of delivery, separates labor management from delivery, and retires global/bundled obstetric CPTs after 1/1/2027.

state_specific_rules: NYS Medicaid MMC/HARP: 0500F and 0503F informational claims

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This anesthesia policy is on-topic for delivery-related episodes because it explicitly includes obstetric anesthesia CPT codes for vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery, cesarean hysterectomy, urgent hysterectomy following delivery, external cephalic version, and neuraxial labor analgesia. Reimbursement is time-based under the standard anesthesia formula, and claims missing the required anesthesia modifier or anesthesia time are rejected or denied.

This is a professional anesthesia policy rather than a DRG payment policy. For delivery-related professional claims, neuraxial labor analgesia/anesthesia for planned vaginal delivery is reimbursed using base units plus time units with a required anesthesia modifier. Obstetric add-on codes 01968 and 01969 may also be reimbursed when applicable, with state-specific limits in Florida and special time-unit handling in Indiana.

utilization_limits: 1 time unit/15 min first hour IN
state_specific_rules: FL: 01967 and 01967+01968 capped at 360 minutes (24 units) for vaginal or cesarean delivery
IN: modifiers may be in any position
IN: 01967 time units are 15-minute blocks in first hour then 60-minute blocks thereafter
FL: combined 01967 and 01968 capped at 360 minutes (24 units)
IN: 01960 time units are 15-minute blocks in first hour then 60-minute blocks thereafter

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Global cesarean obstetrical care is reimbursable when billed with an appropriate ICD-10 diagnosis from the policy list; elective cesarean without a high-risk diagnosis is not denied but paid below the allowable amount.
In Indiana, global obstetrical bundle codes are not covered. OB care must be unbundled, with prenatal care billed separately from delivery and postpartum care.

state_specific_rules: IN: global OB codes not covered

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Apply a professional cesarean edit to 59510, 59514, and 59515: require diagnosis in any position and assistant surgeon modifier present, with assistant surgeon required; otherwise deny. Apply to CA. Peer: Centene, Healthfirst, and United Health all recognize 59510/59514, but United Health applies the strongest cesarean-specific guardrail by requiring assistant surgeon modifier present..

Recommendation 2: Bundle routine obstetrical care into 59510 or 59514 when the same physician or group provides global care, using approximately 13 antepartum visits and 6 weeks postpartum as the default global obstetrical package window; allow exceptions only for a state, contractual, or health plan policy exception. Apply to CA. Exempt: state, contractual, or health plan policy exception. Peer: Centene, Healthfirst, and United Health all recognize 59510/59514, and Centene plus United Health pair these cesarean delivery codes with global OB episode logic rather than separate routine prenatal/postpartum reimbursement..

Recommendation 3: For anesthesia around cesarean delivery, reimburse 01968 and 01969 separately only as add-ons to 01967 when billed on the same date of service or same labor episode with modifier AA, QK, QX, QY, or QZ, and with actual anesthesia time reported separately from 01967. Apply to CA. Exempt: 01968 and 01969 add-on exception. Peer: Healthfirst and United Health both require AA/QK/QX/QY/QZ on 01967/01968/01969 with time-based reporting, and United Health treats 01968/01969 as separate add-ons rather than combined anesthesia time..
